verified.title: train.checkpoint_hours enters the train key, so changing the checkpoint cadence forces a full retrain
verified.detail: Contracts 5.2's `train` table marks `checkpoint_hours` key = **no** ("| checkpoint_hours | float | 2.0 | no | how often last/ is written |", contracts line 3163), and STAGES["train"] lists it in `projection` (schema.py:242) for exactly that reason — `projection` is the cell that carries a stage's non-keyed fields into settings.yaml (compare `sample`/`inject`, whose `projection` is precisely 2.2's minus list). But `_stage_dotted_fields` (schema.py:947-964) expands the bare section name `"train"` in STAGES["train"]["sections"] (schema.py:234) field by field and never subtracts `projection`, so `checkpoint_hours` lands in `fields_of("train", …)` and in the key payload. Effect a later ticket hits: editing how often `last/` is written moves the train directory (GPU days of retraining, 1.7B LoRA is ~98 h per the project's own timing note) and moves every eval key below it, against 3.2 rule 4's insensitivity guarantee. `train` is the only stage affected — every other stage's `projection` entries are disjoint from its `sections` entries. Fix: subtract `STAGES[stage]["projection"]` from the dotted list `fields_of` diffs over.

verdict.reason:
Behaviour reproduces, but the governing rules say the opposite of what the finding claims, and the code is byte-identical to the ticket.

1) Reproduced: `python3 -c "import experimental_settings.schema as S; print([d for d in S._stage_dotted_fields('train') if 'checkpoint' in d])"` -> `['train.checkpoint_hours']`, so a non-default value enters `fields_of('train', …)` and the train key. Confirmed the overlap is unique to train: per-stage `projection ∩ dotted` is empty for sample/build/eval/inject/score, `['train.checkpoint_hours']` for train.

2) The contract's own tie-break rules the other way. Contracts 2.2 (line ~1774): "**Which column is authoritative.** The \"sections read\" column of 2.1 is the list `key` consults; the \"minus\" column here only records *why* those five fields are absent from it". 2.1's train row (line ~1651) is `| train | models.probe, probe, train | …` — the whole `train` section, no field list and no carve-out. 2.2's train row has `—` in the "minus" column, and 3.3 defines fields as "for every field the stage reads whose value differs from the schema default, minus the stage table's \"minus\" list" — an empty minus list subtracts nothing. So 2.1 + 2.2 + 3.3 all put `train.checkpoint_hours` in the train key; only the 5.2 table (line 3163) marks it `no`, and 2.2 names 2.1 as the column that wins that disagreement.

3) 3.2 rule 4 does not say what the finding claims. It reads: "The path does not change when a field the stage does not read changes, when `notes` changes, …". The train stage *does* read `checkpoint_hours` — 1.6 (line ~1473): "`<train run_dir>/last/` … rewritten every `train.checkpoint_hours`". Rule 4 covers unread fields; it makes no promise about a read field.

4) `projection` is not a key-subtraction cell. Ticket 04 line 384 defines it additively, for `freeze` only: "**`freeze`**: the stage projection of 3.4 — the stage table's `sections` plus `projection` plus `projection_generator` …". Contracts 3.4 (line ~2662) lists the projection extras as the non-keyed request fields (`seeds`, `tasks`, `n_tasks`, `pieces`, `replicas`), the inherited `PROBE_TEXT_FIELDS`, and run-time-only `data` — `checkpoint_hours` is not among them. Nothing in ticket or contracts says `fields_of` diffs over `sections` minus `projection`.

5) The implementation is the ticket's literal data. `diff` of issues/04-setting-schema-and-loader.md:206-220 against experimental_settings/schema.py:232-246 differs on one line only (the `data/example.py` / `data/training_data.py` rename), and the two cells at issue — `"sections": ("models.probe", "probe", "train")` and `"projection": ("train.checkpoint_hours",)` — are identical. Ticket wins over contracts (spec.md section 1), so T04 implemented exactly what it was handed. Ticket 04's own key acceptance block (lines 780-813) tests notes-insensitivity, default-restated, lr/eval.risk isolation — and never asserts checkpoint_hours insensitivity.

6) `.scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md` contains no entry for `checkpoint_hours`, `projection` or 5.2's key column (`grep -n checkpoint_hours` over contracts, errata, index, spec and issues 04/05/06 hits only issues/04 lines 89/216/537/888 and contracts 1473/3163).

What is real is a contracts-internal inconsistency: 5.2's `key = no` for `checkpoint_hours` contradicts 2.1/2.2/3.3. That is an errata entry for the owner to rule on, not a defect in the merged code against its governing rule.

verified.title: An inherited models.agent never reaches agent_row, the family resolution or the version list
verified.detail: `_finalize` captures `agent_alias = full["models"]["agent"]` (schema.py:808) and `agent_family = table[agent_alias]["family"]` (schema.py:814), then runs `_apply_inheritance` at schema.py:881 — which can overwrite `full["models"]["agent"]` with the value inherited from the references (5.4 makes `models.agent` an inherited field precisely so a referencing setting need not restate it) — and only afterwards expands the row with the **stale** alias at schema.py:884. Consequences, all silent: `models.agent_row` is a different alias's table row than `models.agent` names, breaking 5.2's definition ("the agent alias's table row expanded") and making 3.3's `models` entry key the wrong row; `_resolve_generation(full, agent_family)` (schema.py:882) fills `generation.effort`/`date` from the wrong family module, so a family whose `EFFORTS` is empty still gets `effort: high` (5.2 says it "stays absent for a family that has no tiers"); and `versions_of` substitutes `{family}` from `agent_row["family"]` (schema.py:1037), folding the wrong `models/agent_models/<family>.py` VERSION into the sample/inject key. Since `models/agent_models/service.py` serves `agent_row["weights"]` off the frozen settings.yaml (6.1, 7.1), a later inject YAML that omits `models.agent` launches vLLM on the wrong weights while `models.agent` says otherwise. Not triggered by the three YAML files shipped today, all of which state `models.agent` in `common:`. Fix: do the role check, the family lookup, the row expansion and the generation resolution after `_apply_inheritance`.

verified.title: data.instructions and the split lists are validated against the pre-inheritance data.env
verified.detail: Same ordering defect as SCHEMA-2 on the other inherited group. `_finalize` reads `env = full["data"]["env"]` at schema.py:790 and uses it for 5.7's `data.instructions` refusal (schema.py:791-795) and for 5.3's per-element split validation against the environment's `splits:` block and `SPLIT_ROLE` (schema.py:797-805); `_apply_inheritance` only replaces `data.env`/`data.instructions` afterwards (schema.py:881). A referencing setting that does not state `data:` therefore has its splits checked against the schema default `appworld` while the setting it actually loads with is the inherited environment. 5.3 states the opposite: "every element of `sample.split` / `inject.split` is validated against the `splits:` block of the chosen `data.env` and against that environment's `SPLIT_ROLE` keys, so a split that environment does not have fails immediately with that environment named". What a later ticket hits: with a second environment registered, an inject setting asking for a split that environment does not have loads cleanly and fails inside `agent/loop.py` after the cards are taken — the exact failure 5.7's instructions bullet says the load-time check exists to prevent.

verified.title: The models.probe-under-inject refusal is checked on raw YAML only, so an override or a sweep sets it and two sweep children collide on one directory
verified.detail: `_check_raw_sections` (schema.py:509-523) implements 2.1/5.7's "a `probe:` section or a `models.probe` field in a setting whose workflow contains `inject`" against the raw `common:`/named dicts only. Unlike the section-for-a-stage-not-in-the-workflow refusal, 5.7 attaches no "evaluated against what the YAML file itself holds" qualifier to this bullet, and neither does 2.1. Both the command-line override path (schema.py:549-558) and the sweep path (`_sweep_children` at schema.py:563-577, whose values are applied with `_set_dotted` at schema.py:540-542) write straight into `full["models"]["probe"]`, which `_merge_one` had deliberately set to None for an inject workflow (schema.py:532). `_finalize` then role-checks the alias and expands `models.probe_row` (schema.py:884-886), so an inject run's frozen settings.yaml asserts a probe backbone that 2.1 says is meaningless there (the two probes come from `inject.probe_score`/`inject.probe_gen`). The sweep form is worse: `models.probe` is not in the inject stage's keyed field list, so both children get the same key and the same run directory, `freeze` sees an identical settings_diff.yaml and takes the merge branch instead of the collision branch, and the second child silently rewrites the first's settings.yaml — breaking 3.2 rule 7 ("Sweep children each get their own path").

Override: S.load(inject.yaml,'p1e1_t080',debug=False,overrides={'models.probe':'qwen17'}) -> "OVERRIDE LOADED -> qwen17 {'role': 'probe', 'family': 'qwen', 'weights': 'qwen3-1.7b-base', 'dtype': 'float32'}" with "key unchanged: True" (3be1681b8e9c both ways), and the frozen inject settings.yaml models block holds 'probe': 'qwen17', 'probe_row': {...}. Sweep: adding `sweep: {models.probe: [qwen06, qwen17]}` gives two children, both keyed 3be1681b8e9c, "same dir: True"; freezing both in order raises nothing (settings_diff.yaml is `inject.theta: 0.8` for both, so freeze at schema.py:1212-1218 takes the merge branch) and the shared settings.yaml ends holding the second child's probe: qwen17, destroying the first child's frozen settings — contradicting 3.2 rule 7 "Sweep children each get their own path". The cited rules say what the finding claims: contracts 5.7 attaches "This one is evaluated against what the YAML file itself holds ... never against the merged setting" only to the "a section for a stage the file's workflow: line does not name" bullet, while the separate bullet "a probe: section or a models.probe field in a setting whose workflow contains inject" carries no qualifier, and 2.1 ("inject reads no models.probe and no probe section") carries none either. Ticket 04 wins over the contracts and rules the same way: schema.py's check is raw-only (_check_raw_sections, schema.py:509-523, called at 899 on common/named), but .scratch/from-zero/issues/04-setting-schema-and-loader.md:145-146 states of the MERGED setting "On a workflow containing `inject`, both `models.probe` and `models.probe_row` are `None`", and its behaviour section says load implements "Every refusal of 5.7". No errata entry scopes this refusal to the raw file (the only override-related entry, contract-errata.md:81, only fixes right-hand-side parsing), and no later ticket defers it; the raw-only scoping is the implementer's own decision recorded in .scratch/from-zero/sdd/2026-09-17-wave2/T04-report.md:357-361, justified by quoting the qualifier that belongs to the other bullet. One qualification: the same-directory collision is a general consequence of sweeping any field the stage does not key (e.g. inject.pieces), not unique to models.probe; ticket 04's C4 battery only exercises the YAML-stated forms, so tightening to the merged setting breaks no stated acceptance output.

minors.title: freeze widens a dotted sections entry to the whole section, so a shared sample directory's settings.yaml flip-flops between owners
minors.detail: `_projection_sections` (schema.py:1176-1186) reduces every STAGES entry to `t.split(".", 1)[0]`, and `freeze` then writes each whole section (schema.py:1195-1198). Contracts 3.4 fixes the projection at field granularity — "`freeze` writes only what *this* stage reads at run time: the sections the stage table names (2.1)" — and 2.1's `sample` cell names `models.agent`, not the whole `models` section. The demonstrated consequence is the one 3.4 spells out for a whole-setting file: two settings that legitimately share a `sample` key (they differ only in the probe alias, which is not in the sample key) both freeze into that one directory; the diff matches so the collision check passes, and the second launch silently rewrites `models.probe`/`models.probe_row` in the first owner's settings.yaml. Kept minor because no reader of a `sample` run's frozen file uses those two fields today — 7.2's render-only probe piece takes `--agent-model <alias>` and echoes only family and weights — but the same widening also puts the whole `probe` section into an `eval` run and the whole `sample`/`inject` sections into a `score` run.

minors.title: Sweep children are returned in cartesian-product order, not name order
minors.detail: `_sweep_children` sorts the swept field names (schema.py:571) but then emits `itertools.product` over the value lists in the order the YAML wrote them (schema.py:573-576), so the returned list is ordered by value position, not by child name. Contracts 5.1 says `load` returns "one element when there is none, the children in name order when there is one", and ticket 04 repeats it ("Returns a list: one element, or the sweep children in name order"). It only looks right in the acceptance suite because the ticket's example lists its values already ascending. What a later ticket hits: `run.py`'s walk iterates this list, and 5.5's rule that "the first child launches [the shared upstream stage] and the rest find the key already running and wait" then depends on YAML value order rather than on the child name a person can predict and type back. Fix: `sorted(out)` on the suffix before returning.

minors.title: Malformed override, sweep and section input raises TypeError/KeyError/AttributeError instead of a SchemaError naming the field
minors.detail: spec.md section 5 requires every refusal to name the field, the file or the value, and 5.7 requires "a key that is not in the schema" and "a `sweep:` ... over a field that is not in the schema" to be loader refusals. Four inputs escape as raw Python exceptions instead: (a) an override whose dotted path descends into a non-mapping — `_get_dotted` (schema.py:478-483) catches only `KeyError` at schema.py:554-556, so indexing a list raises TypeError; (b) the same path through `_sweep_children`, which only validates the first path segment (schema.py:568); (c) a sweep over a field of a section this file's workflow does not name — `_set_dotted` (schema.py:540) raises a bare `KeyError: 'train'`; (d) a YAML section key present with no mapping under it (`models:` on its own line) — `_apply_fields`/`_check_raw_sections` call `.items()`/`.get()` on None. A later ticket hits these through `run.py`'s command line, where the person sees a traceback rather than the field name.

verified.title: split_args' paren walk is quote-blind, so 13 of 4,040 real actions are silently parsed into a truncated call that the round-trip gate cannot catch
verified.detail: `_first_call_named` (appworld.py:89-103) counts `(`/`)` with no quote tracking, so a `)` inside a string literal closes the call early. AppWorld's generated passwords contain `)` and `(` constantly, so this is not hypothetical: over the 315 p1 trajectories, 13 of the 4,040 parsed actions get a span/arg list that stops inside the password string (e.g. `password="TsivP)G"` parses as `('password', 'TsivP')`), and all 10 of the 34 actions the ticket's B4 note attributes to "an api call that never closes its parentheses" are in fact well-formed calls with a `(` inside a string — `complete_call`, which IS quote-aware (appworld.py:232-267, ported from parse_call.py:27-69), balances every one of them. 23 events in all, 0.57% of non-null actions. The truncated 13 are the dangerous half: `build_call` re-writes the truncated args and `split_args` re-reads them identically, so 2.5's round-trip hard stop passes and ticket 09 writes a corrupt ground-truth `example.call` (`apis.spotify.login(username=m@x.com, password=TsivP)`) with no gate, no count and no report line. Eval's `params_all_ok` can never be earned on those rows however right the generation is — exactly the failure 2.5's gate exists to prevent, one layer below the gate. This is ticket-specified behaviour (the ticket pins `first_call_named`, rules.py:152-164, and legacy/pipeline/inject/parse_call.py's own docstring names this exact failure as the reason complete_call was hand-written), so the fix is the owner's call, not a silent implementer change: give `split_args` the same quote/escape/triple-quote walk `complete_call` already carries, and re-measure the B4 counts (the ticket's `4074 4040 4040` and its 24+10 split of the None cases both move).

verified.title: build_call leaves a value with leading or trailing whitespace bare, so split_args strips it back off and the build's round-trip hard stop fires
verified.detail: `_bare_safe` (appworld.py:120-139) tests only for an empty value, a top-level `,` or `=`, and unbalanced brackets/quotes. It does not test for outer whitespace, although `_split_args_named` ends every value with `.strip().strip("\"'")` (appworld.py:82,84) — the whitespace strip happens outside the quotes, so a quoted argument keeps its inner leading/trailing spaces in the value and loses them when the value is written back bare. `build_call` is therefore not the inverse of `split_args` over `split_args`' own output for any value with outer whitespace, and contracts 2.5 makes that a hard stop: "a row whose `call` does not re-parse to its `tool` and `args`" stops the whole build naming the rows. Today's p1 corpus happens to contain no such value (I measured 0 of 4,074 non-null actions), which is why B4 passes 4040/4040; the first collected action of the shape `apis.phone.send_message(message="See you at 5 ")` stops ticket 09's build stage dead. Root-cause fix, one condition: `_bare_safe` returns False when `value != value.strip()`, which sends the value down the existing quoting branch — I verified `apis.a.b(message='hello world ')` round-trips exactly.

minors.title: Probe.forward's generator branch casts the hidden state to float32 before the LM head, so any backbone that is not float32 raises outside autocast
minors.detail: models/probe_models/base.py:96-100 ends the generator branch with `picked = out.last_hidden_state[seq_idx, tok_idx].float()` then `logits = lm_head(picked)`. The `.float()` is correct in the classifier branch (line 93), because `qwen.attach_head` builds the head with `dtype=torch.float32` and it stays float32 through `instance.to(device)`. The LM head is not a separate float32 module: it is part of the backbone and carries the backbone's dtype, so feeding it a float32 activation is a plain dtype mismatch and torch refuses. It cannot fire on today's `models/table.yaml`, whose three probe rows all carry `dtype: float32` (the errata of ticket 06 section 1), and it is masked whenever the caller wraps the call in `torch.autocast`. It fires on a float32 activation against a non-float32 backbone, and there are two live routes to one: contracts 6.1's own example probe row writes `dtype: bfloat16`, so restoring that one word in the owner's data file is enough; and `load`'s restore path deliberately takes `backbone_module.DTYPE` (`qwen.DTYPE = "bfloat16"`, base.py:183-184) on a cuda device. The callers are ticket 13's `train/methods/cgen.py` and `cparam.py`, whose `loss`, `reference_loss` and the 2.6 alignment gate reach the model only through `Probe.forward`; a `predict`/`reference_loss` pass that runs under `no_grad` without an autocast context would crash on the first batch rather than produce a number. Root-cause shape of the fix: apply the LM head at the backbone's own dtype and cast the result, `logits = lm_head(picked).float()`, leaving the classifier branch's cast where it is.
